findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine at the bar would not register sanitizer on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. The bottle of sanitizer hooked into dish machine was running low, so a new sanitizer bottle was hooked up, however the sanitizer would still not register on either test strips. Discussed with PIC, Ecolab will be contacted to service machine. Triple sink at the bar will be set up and used for any bar dish washing needed. Follow-up issued for 8/20/24. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed a box of food to be resting under a leak in the walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, boxes were relocated away from leak. Ensure food is being protected and checked at a frequency that prevents contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed multiple whisks to be hanging in contact with wall next to the back prep table. Discussed with PIC, whisks were put through the wash, rinse, sanitize process and relocated with the other utensils. Ensure all clean utensils are being stored in a way that prevents contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Observed the bar hand sink to be leaking. Discussed with PIC, plumber was contacted to service hand sink. Ensure all plumbing repairs are handled by a licensed plumber, and that all sinks are properly draining. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Observed the sprinkler system in the walk in freezer to be leaking. A 6 inch icicle has formed from sprinkler. Discussed with PIC, a technician shall be contacted to service sprinkler system. Ensure repairs are made to sprinkler system to meet manufacturer’s standards. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Multiple employees are observed to change gloves without washing hands. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to review as needed with employees when hand washing is needed. Ensure that hand washing takes place during glove changes.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The dish machine in the bar would not register sanitizer on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. As the jug of sanitizer is observed clear it is believed that the concentrate has off gassed to a level where it is no longer effective. This was discussed with the PIC and bar manager. The three part sink will be used for the sanitize step in this area tonight (sink observed at 200 ppm CL) and a new jug will be acquired prior to re-opening the facility. A follow -up is being set for the next available day (Monday) to ensure compliance.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

Multiple tubs are observed storing utensils and the tubs have accumulated food debris/dust. Ensure that these items are cleaned regularly so as to ensure that the food contact surfaces are maintained clean until use.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

At the time of this inspection none of the CFPMs available have completed their allergen training. They are instructed to have allergen training available for all of the CFPMs prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the bar soda nozzle holder to have a layer of white film/mold accumulation/slime. Discussed with PIC and bar tender. Ensure staff is aware to clean the soda nozzle holder, as well as the nozzles themselves. Bar tender washed, rinsed, and sanitized on site. COS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed the bar area to be using a quaternary ammonium spray bottle, but utilizing in-use rags to wipe down surfaces. Discussed paper towel versus rag use. Rags should be used with sanitizer buckets and kept immersed when not being utilized. Buckets should be changed out frequently so sanitizer remains active in concentration. Paper towels should be used for spay bottles of sanitizer. PIC was in compliance to change the process to either rags and buckets at the bar and/or paper towels and spray bottles. Ensure changes are made and staff is aware of new process.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

(REPEAT) Observed stacks of wet cup as at the server soda station. Cease practice. Discussed with PIC. Ensure dish washer/bar tenders/servers are aware that cups should not be stacked wet. Cups should be air dried prior to stacking. Correct by next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/30/23.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. The walk-in cooler fan has dust.
2. Interior of fryers and sides of the equipment are heavily soiled in grease debris and accumulation.
3. The metal cart next the 3 compartment sink needs power washed - significant food splash on the cart. Cart is used for dirty dish ware. 
4. Dish machine has a heavy amount of lime build-up within the machine (interior and on the inside of the doors). Delime dish machine as needed to prevent build-up.
5. The wall near the pizza prep table (in between hand sink and pizza prep) has a storage shelf with onions. The wall behind it has food splash on the wall.
6. The beer walk-in cooler has milk and dressings being stored in it. The fans in this cooler are dusty.

Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure employees are aware to clean and pay particular attention to the above areas. #1-4 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 1/30/23. Clean the above locations before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the kitchen to have many small holes that need caulked still. Repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/30/23. Walk around the kitchen with caulking and fill all visible holes in the wall. Correct before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

Observed no soap at the bar hand sink. Bartender provided soap upon request as Inspector attempted to wash hands. Ensure all hand sinks have a supple of soap readily available to properly wash hands. Discussed with bartender and employees. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact areas in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. The panini makers (2x) in the kitchen have a large amount of grease and food debris build-up on the backs (where the hinges are). 
2. Interior of bottom prep coolers have food debris on ledges and lips inside. 
3. Bottom reach-in freezer near breading station has food debris on base of interior of cooler.
4. The shelving unit across from the fryers (next to breading station) has a large amount of grease and food splash on the shelving. Clean utensils are being stored on this shelving unit. The grates of the shelving unit need cleaned and any food equipment should be re-washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

Discussed routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff is cleaning to avoid food splash, debris, and grease build-up. Inspector will follow-up on 2/8/23 regarding cleaning the above areas.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed salmon to be thawed within the reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Discussed new methods with PIC and kitchen employees. Salmon should be removed from packaging prior to thawing as the label states on the ROP packaging. Employees were in compliance. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple coolers to lack thermometers. Discussed purchasing extra thermometers to have on hand for the coolers. They are easily misplaced or broken within coolers. PIC indicated he would purchase thermometers and make sure to keep extras on site. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple areas in the kitchen with to-go single-service food containers and regular plates/bowls to not be flipped over to prevent cross contamination. Ensure food- and lip-contact areas are turned upside down to prevent contamination. Inspector corrected several areas. Ensure staff is aware of this and changes practices. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

Observed stacks of wet cups in the bar area and the server soda station. Cease practice. Ensure dish washer, bar tender, and employees are aware not to stack cups wet and allow cups to air dry prior to stacking. Discussed with employees and PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. The wall next to the breading station has food splash on it. The air vent in this area needs dusted as well.
2. The walk-in cooler fan has dust.
3. Interior of fryers need cleaned - heavy grease accumulation.
4. Baffles/hood system are slightly soiled. Facility utilizes C.F.B., Inc. for cleaning and services are twice a year. Inspector suggested perhaps increasing the cleaning services to 3x yearly due to amount of deep frying the facility does. Employees can also clean the hood system between professional services.
5. The metal cart near the 3 compartment sink needs power washed. Heavy amount of food splash on the cart. Cart is used for dirty dishes in this area.
6. Dish machine has a heavy amount of lime build-up within the machine (interior and on the inside of the doors). Delime the dish machine as needed to prevent build-up.
7. Mop sink area next to dish machine has a heavy amount of black mold on the walls and basin. Clean the walls and mop sink. Caulk the mop sink again if needed due to mold.

Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff stays on a cleaning schedule to prevent debris/grease/food splash build-up. Clean the above areas before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following places that are in need of repairs to make smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent:
1. The prep sink near the the spices in the kitchen (between hand sink and pizza prep area) needs caulked to the wall.
2. Many small holes throughout the walls of the kitchen. Walk around the kitchen and caulk all holes. 
3. The 3 compartment sink has molded caulking. Remove the caulking and re-caulk the 3 compartment sink to the wall. Water exposure has caused the mold.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed multiple CFPM’s to lack allergen training certification. Provided educational hand out. Ensure all certified food protection manager’s complete allergen training. Certification is valid for 3 years. Some allergen certifications were also expired. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the bar area is without a method of drying hands after washing. Paper towels were supplied during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

The drain line for the four part sink in the bar area is observed to be leaking during the inspection. Inspector discussed with the PIC and they are aware that it needs repair prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Multiple locations around the facility are observed in need of cleaning during the inspection: 1) the shelf between the pizza prep cooler and the seasonings has a section with oil build up observed (corrected on site); 2) the wall next to the battering station has food splash on it; 3) the metal shelf over the pizza prep station has dust/ general debris; 4) the shelf along the northern section of the food prep area has significant grease build up on the bottom two shelves. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to prevent build up. PIC stated that the shelves on the north of the kitchen are planned on being replaced. They should remain clean until then.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. 

On arrival, the dish machine in the facility would not register sanitizer on either the inspector’s or the facility’s test strips. PIC contacted EcoLab and the rep stated that they would be to the facility by 4 pm to conduct maintenance. Until then, the facility is using the dish machine for cleaning and rinsing dishes, then letting them sit in sanitizer in the three part sink. As they are doing this, the violation is being corrected at this time and the inspector will SPOT CHECK next week for maintenance on the dish machine sanitizer.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Fish are observed in an ice bath (1/2 pan inside of a 1/2 pan) to be holding between 39-50 degrees F. Ice was observed to only be making contact with the bottom of the container. Discussed with the kitchen manager and the pans were changed so that the level of ice will be above the food level moving foreword. PIC stated that the fish was out approximately 1 hour from a cooler. Inspector instructed for the remaining fish from the current half pan be placed in a cooler for rapid return to cold holding limits.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. The nozzles on both front fountain drink machines are observed with an accumulation of gunk inside the nozzles. PIC was consulted and the nozzles replaced with clean. Dirty ones were moved to cleaning.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11 Cleaned equipment and utensils shall be stored in a way to prevent contamination. Bus tubs used to store cleaned/ sanitized utensils along the north side of the kitchen are observed soiled. Containers should be maintained clean to prevent recontamination of utensils. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to maintain clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) A food employee was observed conducting general bar tasks, then move directly to wrapping silverware without washing hands. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Education tool place to correct.

PIC is instructed to clean the locations often enough so as to prevent the accumulation of food debris/grease.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee was observed to not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. PIC was informed and directed to review proper hand washing with the employees.

The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment are not soiled prior to use. The containers and utensils were moved to the dish area for cleaning.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) 1) The fan blowing towards the food prep areas was observed soiled with dust. 2) The sandwich prep cooler was observed with food debris around the edges usually hidden by the lid. PIC was instructed to clean the non-food contact surfaces often enough to prevent them from becoming significantly soiled.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) The shelves in the walk in cooler were observed soiled. Clean the shelves often enough so as to prevent them from becoming soiled.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110  (C) Multiple employee foods were observed stored in the walk in cooler behind foods intended for consumers. The containers of these foods were also observed to have mold beginning to grow on them. PIC discarded the containers during the inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

2-301.14 (E) (P) Employees shall clean their hands immediately before engaging in food preparation or before handling cleaned and sanitized utensils.

An employee was observed to handle soiled dishes and switch to cleaned dishes and back without washing their hands. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to review procedures with employees in relation to when to wash hands.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2)  (P) TCS foods shall be held at 41 F or less to control for the growth of pathogenic organisms.

House made buffalo ranch sauce was observed to be at 47 F internal temperature (probed) in the bottom of the prep cooler used for pizza preparation. Proper cold holding was discussed with the PIC and the sauce was discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed can heavily dented along top seam. Manager discarded can and will return for credit with supplier.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed caulk along back of sink in employee restroom to be cracked. Re-caulk this surface to make smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - Non-food equipment exposed to splash or frequint cleaning shall be designed and fabricated so as to be smooth, washable, free of unessicary ledges, projections, or crevices.

findings.comment:

Observed mold in nozzle of soda fountain. Clean nozzles routinly.

750-800e All non-food contact surfaces shall be properly cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Right side of fryer soiled and not regularly cleaned. Routinely clean this area.
Vent cover of cooler under flat top has accumulation of dust. Routinely clean the vent cover.
Conveyor oven soiled with food debris. Clean routinely to avoid accumulation of food debris. This is a repeat violation.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.comment:
Observed single service items (foam trays and plastic lids) to be stored with food contact surface facing up. Invert items to keep food surface clean.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.
